newsitem.title: USA: Dell PC sales via Internet doubling.
newsitem.headline: Dell PC sales via Internet doubling.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Michael Dell said the company's sales of personal computers over the Internet continue to explode and are now approaching an annual run rate of $500 million.
He said in a keynote address at the PC Expo trade show that Dell's daily Internet sales are doubling to about $2 million at present from $1 million in recent months.

"So get out your credit cards and go to www.dell.com," he joked. "Dell.com brings us closer to our customers...The Internet is turbo-charging the efficiency of Dell's direct model." Customers configure their own PCs at Dell's Web site.

Dell said more than 5,000 Dell customers now have developed personalized Web pages that provide faster access to information and enable customers to configure products online and monitor the status of their orders.
Dell said the company's component suppliers will begin to benefit with a window onto Dell's factory show floors via the World Wide Web and links to Dell with Internet technology.

Dell and another Dell executive said the Net PC, introduced by many PC makers on Monday, including Dell, will be used by a "narrow market" and that more users want so-called "managed PCs," which are more flexible.
